claims.claim: A foreign resident living in Korea 5 years or less of the last 10 is taxed on foreign-source income only when paid by a Korean entity or transferred to Korea; after that, worldwide

sources.name: PwC: Korea, taxes on personal income
sources.says: Last reviewed 02 July 2026. Top rate 45% on taxable income of KRW 1 billion and above; local income tax "at a rate of 10% of the PIT rates". Foreign residents with 5 years or less of residence in the last 10 are "taxed on Korea-source income"; foreign-source income is reportable only if a Korean entity pays it or it is transferred to Korea.

claims.claim: Interest and dividends above KRW 20m a year join the progressive scale up to 45% plus 10% local tax (about 49.5%)

sources.name: PwC: Korea, income determination
sources.says: Last reviewed 02 July 2026. Most Korean-source dividends and interest are withheld at 15.4%; "Financial income over KRW 20 million a year is included in global income." Gains on foreign shares are carved out of its foreign-assets rule and given no rate.

sources.name: PwC: Korea, taxes on personal income
sources.says: Last reviewed 02 July 2026. Top rate 45% on taxable income of KRW 1 billion and above; local income tax "at a rate of 10% of the PIT rates". Foreign residents with 5 years or less of residence in the last 10 are "taxed on Korea-source income"; foreign-source income is reportable only if a Korean entity pays it or it is transferred to Korea.

sources.name: Toss Bank: comprehensive taxation of financial income
sources.says: Cites NTS sources accessed 2026.04.03. "원천 징수되지 않은 금융소득은 금액과 관계없이 종합과세 대상이 될 수 있어요"; of overseas interest and dividends: "이런 소득은 기준 이하라도 종합과세 대상이 될 수 있어요."

also: summary: "(dividends above KRW 20m at up to about 49.5%)" -> "(dividends at up to about 49.5%)"
claims.note: The KRW 20m threshold and the rates are confirmed. What the profile left out matters to its reader: dividends from a US broker are not withheld in Korea, and income not withheld at source "can be" comprehensively taxed whatever the amount (Toss Bank, citing the NTS). The tax fact keeps its wording and adds the case; the summary's threshold went. A Korean primary page was not read (PwC Korea's One Point Tax returned HTTP 403). Tax score stays 2.

claims.claim: From 2027 an exit tax reaches foreign shares worth more than KRW 500m in total for anyone resident 5 of the last 10 years who emigrates

sources.name: KPMG GMS Flash Alert 2026-066: Korea exit tax extended to overseas stocks
sources.says: Dated 11 March 2026. "Following recent legislative amendments", from departures on or after 1 January 2027 the exit tax covers overseas stocks for people resident at least five of the ten years before departure; "the major shareholder condition will not be applicable to overseas stocks"; holdings worth KRW 500 million or less in total are exempt; exemptions for foreign workers need 80% of the 10 years in Korean employment.

claims.note: The foreign-worker exemptions need 80% of the 10 years in Korean employment, so they do not reach a retiree.
claims.modelMismatch: localTaxes.ts has no South Korea entry (the plan already notes it); the 2027 exit tax on foreign shares over KRW 500m is not modelled.

"If the deceased was a resident of Korea at the time of death, inheritance tax applies to worldwide assets"; "For non-residents, only assets situated in Korea are subject to inheritance tax"; rates "range from 10% to 50%", "50% for inheritances exceeding 3 billion KRW"; a general deduction "up to 500 million KRW" for residents.
